articles.title: Presidente do BC paraguaio renuncia após crise financeira no Ueno Bank | G1
articles.standfirst: Maior emissor de cartões de crédito do Paraguai tem cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e é alvo de investigações. Caso também aumenta a pressão sobre o governo de Santiago Peña.
articles.summary: Maior emissor de cartões de crédito do Paraguai tem cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e é alvo de investigações. Caso também aumenta a pressão sobre o governo de Santiago Peña.
articles.body:
Vista aérea mostra a sede do Ueno Bank, em Assunção, no Paraguai. — Foto: Reuters

Uma crise envolvendo o banco digital Ueno , que tem cerca de 3 milhões de clientes no Paraguai, levou à renúncia de Carlos Carvallo, presidente do Banco Central do país, nesta terça-feira (3). Além disso, aumentou a pressão sobre o governo do presidente Santiago Peña.

A instituição financeira, maior emissora de cartões de crédito do Paraguai, enfrenta problemas financeiros e é alvo de investigações . Após ajustes em seus balanços, o índice de solvência do banco (que mede sua capacidade de pagamento) caiu para menos da metade do mínimo exigido.

Diante da situação, o Banco Central iniciou um procedimento para proteger os depositantes e limitar possíveis impactos sobre o sistema financeiro. O Ministério Público também pediu a abertura de uma investigação criminal sobre o caso e determinou a prisão de oito pessoas ligadas ao Ueno.

Nos últimos meses, o banco já vinha sob maior fiscalização. Órgãos reguladores investigavam se o Ueno havia financiado indiretamente a venda de uma carteira de ativos de uma empresa ligada ao Grupo Vázquez, seu controlador. O banco negava a operação.

O caso também trouxe desgaste para o governo de Peña e ameaça a reputação do Paraguai como um dos destinos emergentes da América do Sul para o capital estrangeiro, grande parte dele proveniente do Brasil.

Foi nesse contexto que o presidente paraguaio pediu a renúncia de Carvallo. O chefe do BC comandou o próprio Ueno até agosto de 2023. Tanto ele quanto o Banco Central vinham sendo criticados por parlamentares pela supervisão da instituição.

Peña também teve ligação com o grupo controlador do Ueno, do qual foi sócio até março de 2025.

O Ueno administra aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em recursos públicos no Paraguai. Nesta terça, clientes foram a agências do banco, mas encontraram as portas fechadas. Entre eles estavam aposentados que recebem benefícios do governo por meio do Ueno.

“Estamos exigindo acesso ao dinheiro que temos aqui no banco Ueno”, disse à agência Reuters Manuel Cáceres, morador de Ñemby, nos arredores de Assunção. “Infelizmente, muita gente, inclusive eu, está passando a manhã assim.”

Diante da crise, Peña anunciou um acordo com líderes do Congresso para acelerar a votação de um projeto que autoriza o uso do Fundo de Garantia do país para fazer pagamentos aos depositantes.

O presidente paraguaio afirmou ainda que a medida deve assegurar a devolução de recursos públicos, incluindo valores mantidos pelo instituto de seguridade social IPS e por outros fundos públicos de previdência.

Segundo o Banco Central do Paraguai, o caso do Ueno é isolado e não indica problemas mais amplos no sistema financeiro do país.

Peña também buscou afastar esse risco: “Este é um caso específico de uma entidade, não do sistema financeiro nacional.”

O presidente paraguaio acrescentou que os responsáveis pelo caso “devem responder perante o Judiciário, sem exceções e sem privilégios”.

Segundo o BC, a Superintendência de Bancos vai nomear auditores para verificar a situação dos ativos do Ueno.

Carvallo afirmou que permanecerá no cargo durante o procedimento adotado pelas autoridades para lidar com a crise do Ueno.

Ao anunciar a saída, ele disse que a decisão ajudaria a reduzir a controvérsia em torno do Banco Central e permitiria que a instituição e a Superintendência de Bancos trabalhassem sem as disputas políticas e a repercussão na imprensa.

As críticas já haviam levado parlamentares a pedir a demissão da cúpula do BC, depois que eles rejeitaram um relatório sobre o Ueno por considerá-lo incompleto.

O caso também teve reflexos nos mercados. As preocupações com o Ueno pressionaram os títulos em dólar do banco com vencimento em 2031 e os próprios títulos da dívida do Paraguai.

Controlado majoritariamente pelo Grupo Vázquez, o Ueno passou rapidamente de uma fintech local de nicho a um banco de médio porte, em uma trajetória semelhante à de plataformas digitais como Monzo e Nubank.

* Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters

In a post on X, Cramer said that investors are piling "negativity" onto the three tech stocks and that it is "pretty thick."

"No matter what they say, it isn't enough…" he added.

articles.title: US factory orders beat expectations in September amid broad strength
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - New orders for US factory goods increased more than expected in September, boosted by bookings for aircraft and a range of othe...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - New orders for US factory goods increased more than expected in September, boosted by bookings for ‌aircraft and a range of other goods, government data showed ‌on Tuesday.

Factory orders rose 1.8% after an upwardly revised 0.3% gain in August, the ​Commerce Department's Census Bureau said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast orders surging 1.2% after a previously reported 0.1% gain in August.

Orders advanced 7.2% on a year-over-year basis in September.

An artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout and ‌strong consumer spending are ⁠anchoring manufacturing, which accounts for about 9.4% of the economy.

But economists have cautioned that rising interest rates and ⁠declining inflation-adjusted household income would hamper manufacturing activity next year, especially the segments not exposed to the AI spending frenzy.

Though an Institute for Supply ​Management survey ​on Monday showed production at factories ​booming in October, sentiment among ‌manufacturers continued to deteriorate, with pricing volatility, longer lead times, tariffs and the US-Israeli war with Iran cited as major drags.

Factory orders in September were driven by 28.3% jump in bookings for the volatile civilian aircraft and parts component. Orders for motor vehicle bodies, parts ‌and trailers edged up 0.1%. Machinery orders ​soared 1.5%. Orders for computers and electronic ​products rose 0.8%, and ​vaulted 14.9% year over year.

Orders for electrical equipment, appliances ‌and components fell 0.3%. The Census ​Bureau also reported ​that orders for non-defense capital goods excluding aircraft, which are seen as a measure of business spending plans on equipment, increased ​0.6% in September ‌instead of 0.5% as reported last month.

Shipments of these so-called ​core capital goods shot up 1.2% as initially estimated.

(Reporting by ​Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

articles.title: What a Democratic sweep could mean for stocks — and why history says not much
articles.summary: Every midterm outcome under a Republican president has left the S&P 500 about 15% higher a year later.
articles.body:
Polls and prediction markets have spent weeks pointing to a Democratic sweep. History says the outcome has shaped stocks for about three months, then barely at all.

That may surprise anyone bracing for a long night of maps and swing counties. Polymarket gave Democrats a 76% chance of winning both the House and the Senate as of Tuesday morning, with a Democratic House and a Republican Senate a distant second at 19%.

The House looks like the surer bet. The Senate is where the drama is. Republicans hold it 53-47, Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and polling models and prediction markets differ more on that chamber . Some races may not be called Tuesday night.

Since 1946, midterms under a Republican president have ended three of the four ways Congress can go. A year later, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) was up an average of 15% to 16% after each one, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from the Election Day close. Over the long run, Wall Street's verdict has been bipartisan.

The short run is a different story. After the seven midterms that left Democrats running Congress, stocks rose an average of 11% over the next three months and were higher every time. After the lone Republican hold, in 2002, stocks fell 8% as the US moved toward war with Iraq. By the end of each president's term, all three outcomes were up on average.

None of this carries much statistical muscle. A Democratic sweep has happened seven times under a Republican president, a Democratic House with a Republican Senate twice, and a Republican hold once. A Republican House with a Democratic Senate has never happened.

Even the sweep record needs a footnote. In five of those seven years, Democrats already ran Congress. Only twice did a Republican president lose both chambers, as Democrats are trying to make happen this year — in 1954 under Dwight Eisenhower and in 2006 under George W. Bush. Stocks rose about 33% and 7% over the following year.

And the ride can get bumpy. The last time President Trump lost the House, in 2018, the S&P 500 sank nearly 15% by Christmas Eve as the Federal Reserve raised rates and trade tensions with China escalated. Then it bounced, finishing about 12% higher a year after the midterm election. The 2006 sweep by Democrats ran into the financial crisis, leaving stocks down about 38% by the time Bush left office in 2009.

Blue, red or divided, the S&P 500 was higher a year after all 20 midterms since 1946, measured from Election Day, with an average gain of about 14%. The closest call was 1946 itself, a gain of just 0.1%. The streak lines up with the strongest stretch of the presidential cycle , which runs from late in a midterm year into the next.

articles.title: Betting on US midterms brings rush, stress as serious money goes on the line
articles.summary: (Corrects description of Poser's book to note it is partly about prediction markets, and his trading model to drop reference to Wall Street career, both in f...
articles.body:
(Corrects description of Poser's book to note it is partly about prediction markets, and his trading model to drop reference to Wall Street career, both in fourth paragraph)

By Suzanne McGee, Douglas Gillison and Chris Prentice

NEW YORK, Nov 3 (Reuters) - When polls close in the US midterm elections on Tuesday night, Noah Poser will ‌be glued to his phone tracking dozens of large wagers he placed on prediction markets.

Poser, 28, who works in financial technology and has written about betting strategies in ‌such markets, plans to track every change in the vote count from a friend's watch party in New York City.

He said he has wagers with a total value in the six figures on the line, betting on a strong showing by Democrats, ​and entered the bets a few months ago when odds were at a much better price. If he wins, he estimates profits of as much as $30,000.

"It's a numbers game; you have to strip your emotions out of it," said Poser, the author of a self-published book about his betting strategies, including prediction markets. Poser built a proprietary quantitative model for trading these markets.

He will not be alone on Tuesday evening. Across the United States, people are betting on this year's midterm races at record levels for US election betting.

Prediction markets rose to prominence in 2024 when they bucked traditional opinion polls in signaling that Donald Trump ‌would win the presidency. The platforms allow traders to buy and ⁠sell "yes" or "no" contracts on an array of race outcomes and variables, and there is more than $1.4 billion wagered on the midterms, according to the platforms and industry research.

Among those placing bets is Darius Gamble, 51, in Gardendale, Alabama, who said he has been betting on the platforms ⁠for two or three months but won't wager more than $20 on anything.

"It is gambling, just disguised as predictions," said Gamble, who is a human resources business partner. "It gives you a gambling rush."

Another hopeful with money on the line is Yadin Eldar, a 22-year-old student at Florida State University.

While he anticipates large-scale Democratic victories, Eldar is opting for a contrarian strategy by placing bets on races where his analysis shows the odds of Republican ​candidates ​emerging victorious are "extremely underpriced."

"You can make a 50-55% profit on Republicans winning in Florida," he said in an interview.

Still, ​betting on elections is stressful, said Eldar, who may leave his own ‌phone at home when he heads to an unrelated birthday party on Tuesday night.

articles.title: BMW issues second profit warning in a year
articles.summary: Premium German carmaker BMW issued its second profit warning for the financial year on Tuesday, citing costs related to job cuts as well as a production ramp...
articles.body:
Premium German carmaker BMW issued its second profit warning for the financial year on Tuesday, citing costs related to job cuts as well as a production ramp-up.

The core profit margin at the cars business was now seen at between minus 0.5 percent to plus 0.5 percent in 2026, BMW said, meaning it could make an operating loss in its key activity.

That compares to a core profit margin of between one and three percent which the Munich-based manufacturer expected back in June, itself a cut on expectations at the start of the year.

Like its peers, BMW has struggled with cutthroat competition and falling demand in China, the world's largest car market.

Competitors Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen have both also issued profit warnings this year and, like BMW, plan job cuts to bring costs down.

In its latest warning, BMW said its redundancy program was moving faster than expected, resulting in bigger-than-anticipated severance payments for the final quarter of the year.

"The company intends to leverage the momentum generated by its workforce restructuring program to expand its organizational and process realignment more quickly," it said.

"The reduction in management functions will be implemented faster than announced," it added.

Strong demand for new models based on the firm's Neue Klasse platform meanwhile meant the company would incur charges to bring in extra shifts, it said.

Car and motorbike deliveries for the year are nevertheless expected to fall more steeply than expected, BMW said.

Across its brands -- which apart from the namesake include Mini and Rolls-Royce -- BMW last year delivered a total 2.46 million vehicles.

BMW reports its results for the third quarter on Wednesday.

articles.title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount
articles.summary: The new ad placements could help Reddit squeeze more revenue from existing users as Google's AI search changes how people discover its content.
articles.body:
Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it's beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform.

"Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user's search query," Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. "This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time."

The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for "espresso station" might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for "home office setup" could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs.

The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web's landscape, and subsequently its reach.

Despite beating Wall Street's estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company's stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week , with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit's declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google's move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers' websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google's Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites.

Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter.

This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S.

articles.title: Supermicro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook
articles.summary: Supermicro reported its Q1 earnings after the bell Tuesday.
articles.body:
Data center infrastructure company Supermicro ( SMCI ) reported its fiscal first quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated outlook for Q2.

The company said it anticipates Q2 sales of between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion. Analysts were calling for $16.35 billion.

Supermicro stock rose more than 5% immediately following the news.

"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027," CEO Charles Liang said in a statement.

"[Data Center Building Block Solutions] is driving significant value for our customers — from gigawatt-scale data centers down to single-container PODs — which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, with superior uptime and more cost-effective for our customer base."

For the quarter, the company reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.81 and revenue of $19.95 billion, well ahead of Wall Street's projections and the company's preliminary results.

Gross margins topped 12.8%, also topping Supermicro's preliminary numbers of between 12% and 12.5%.

Supermicro stock fell a staggering 27% over the last month after Gartner issued a report saying that 80% of neocloud companies would cease operations by 2030 due to a lack of a return on invested capital.

Neoclouds CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) plunged on the news and are down 40% and 37%, respectively, in the last month. CoreWeave is a Supermicro customer.

Supermicro stock has had a rough year, plummeting 38% over the last 12 months on questions about its profitability.

articles.title: Palantir is the latest victim of investors' sky-high earnings expectations
articles.summary: Investors were punishing a slowdown in commercial bookings in the quarter, even as the rest of the tech darling's Q3 report was upbeat on most metrics.
articles.body:
Palantir stock dropped Tuesday even after it delivered strong Q3 results.

Shares of the data softare firm are struggling against wider tech jitters and shifting investor sentiment.

Views on its results are mixed on Wall Street, even as the company continues to grow.

Investors are hammering Palantir stock on Tuesday, dumping shares even after the AI-powered data software firm delivered strong third-quarter earnings.

Shares of the company fell as much as 7% to $165.25 before rebounding to end the day down about 2.5%. Palantir beat Wall Street's estimates on key metrics in the quarter, and reported that commercial revenue exceeded revenue from government contracts for the first time. Total revenue of $2.31 billion blew past analysts' expectations.

However, a sharp slowdown in commercial bookings compared to the second quarter rattled investors' view of the stock. The firm reported year over year commercial bookings growth of 11%, compared to 153% booking growth in the prior quarter.

"Analysts blamed a deceleration in US commercial bookings for the selloff, which has taken the stock down to support around $165," David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, said. "These are all indications that there's some fragility spreading across the AI-adjacent trade."

It's the latest example of a hiccup in an otherwise rosy earnings report derailing a high-flying tech stock. Palantir's move is emblematic of just how high investors' expectations have risen, to the point where shares sell off at the first sign of trouble.

Other tech giants know well already, with hyperscalers and other AI builders under intense scrutiny when it comes to things like capex spending , which can overshadow other bright spots in earnings reports.

The tech trade has also weakened broadly in recent weeks. Volatility throughout Asian markets , spanning China, Japan, and South Korea, has led to heightened concern that the AI bubble may be about to pop .

Luke Lango, chief technology analyst at InvestorPlace noted that while his team is still bullish on Palantir, the company doesn't just have to prove its doing well — it has to continuously justify its premium valuation.

"Palantir's rearview looks spectacular, while the view through the windshield got a little foggier after bookings cooled sharply from last quarter's record," Lango said. "For most stocks, that's a footnote. For a stock priced for perfection, it's the headline bears have been waiting for."

Others have highlighted the threat that rising competition could pose, particularly as compute costs continue rising .

articles.title: Pre-Diwali fireworks: Sensex up over 2.4k points in two days
articles.summary: MUMBAI: For the second consecutive session on Tuesday, sensex notched up over a 1,000-point gain as relatively softer crude oil prices, strong foreign
articles.body: MUMBAI: For the second consecutive session on Tuesday, sensex notched up over a 1,000-point gain as relatively softer crude oil prices, strong foreign fund buying, softening yields in the US and a strengthening rupee helped investor sentiment on Dalal Street. After opening on a sound footing, sensex rallied through the session to close 1,225 points or 1.6% up at 76,918 points.Combined with a 1,233-point gain on Monday, the index is now up 2,458 points or 3.3%, the index's best two-day gaining streak since April 8 this year. The gains came on the back of nearly Rs 10,000-crore net buying by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in the secondary market in two sessions.On Tuesday, sensex opened the session up about 600 points, touched an intraday high of 77,093 points (up 1,400 points) and closed just a tad off that level at 76,918 points. On NSE, Nifty too followed a similar trajectory and closed at 23,811 points, up 370 points or 1.6%. Ahead of Diwali this weekend, Tuesday was the fourth straight session of gains for the index.According to Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth, domestic markets rallied sharply as the easing West Asia conflict and falling crude oil prices coupled with encouraging Q2 earnings by corporates buoyed investor sentiment. "Despite weak global cues, domestic equities witnessed frenzied buying while fresh FII buying over the past two sessions and the rupee's recovery against the dollar provided impetus to the market."During the day, Brent crude prices fell to about the $103-per-barrel level, down 1.3%. Last week, Brent hit the $117 level, which in turn had weakened the rupee to near the 96-to-a-dollar mark. On Tuesday, the rupee strengthened 16 paise to close at 94.73 to the dollar.On Tuesday, net buying by foreign funds in the secondary market was at Rs 6,837 crore, exchange data showed. Domestic funds, on the other hand, were net sellers at Rs 3,679 crore. The day's strong foreign fund inflow came on the back of a Rs 3,115 crore net inflow in stocks on Monday. The day's strong gains in the market added about Rs 4.5 lakh crore to investors' wealth, with the aggregate market capitalisation of companies listed on BSE now at Rs 486.8 lakh crore, exchange data showed.HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Bharti Airtel contributed the most to the day's gain in the index.You use AI every day. articles.title: Won't open up dairy sector or let in genetically modified products: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With India, US close to finalising a trade, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Tuesday said India has never opened up its dairy sector
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With India, US close to finalising a trade, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Tuesday said India has never opened up its dairy sector in any free trade agreement and will not allow imports of genetically modified products, describing both as "very sensitive" issues for the country.Addressing students of Kirori Mal College, Goyal said India has "never ever" compromised on any sensitive item and has always protected its farmers, fishermen, and MSMEs in trade pacts."We are sensitive to opening up to certain agricultural produce, certain goods that we are very strong on like marine products. We are very sensitive to opening our dairy. In fact, till date, we have never opened up dairy for anybody. We are very sensitive not to allow any genetically modified products to come to India and we have never allowed it and we'll never allow it in the future," he said.He said, "We are sensitive to our religious sensitivities. So very often in foreign countries, they use calf meat or Rennet while producing their dairy products. We don't allow that in India. It is strictly got to be certified... so that religious sensitivities of the large parts of India are not hurt."Rennet is an enzyme used in cheese-making, traditionally obtained from the stomach lining of young calves. articles.title: SBI net rises 14% to 23k crore, shares slip 1.8%
articles.summary: MUMBAI: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore, driven by a 14.7% increase in net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore and
articles.body: MUMBAI: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore, driven by a 14.7% increase in net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore and lower loan loss provisions. Net interest margin improved to 3.1% from just over 3% a year ago, while loan loss provisions fell 33% to Rs 2,759 crore as asset quality improved.However, the bank's shares fell 1.8% to Rs 969 as investors were disappointed with the 7.3% growth in operating profit to Rs 34,226 crore. The increase was held back by a 24% decline in other income to Rs 11,777 crore.Addressing newspersons, SBI chairman CS Setty reiterated the bank's guidance of 10-11% deposit growth and 14-15% credit growth. The bank has a corporate loan pipeline of Rs 7.8 lakh crore, he said."If nominal GDP growth is around 12 to 12.5%, normally the SBI credit growth rate is 3 to 4% over that and that is where the guidance of 14 to 15% is coming from," explained Setty.The bank does not face any immediate compulsion to raise deposit rates, given its comfortable liquidity position. SBI had excess statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) holdings of more than Rs 4 lakh crore as of Sept 30, providing adequate headroom to fund credit growth, he said.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Government could abolish long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax across investor categories even keeping its fiscal consolidation road map largely unaffected, as the resulting revenue loss is likely to be limited to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY28, a report said on Tuesday.The report from SBI Research estimated that eliminating LTCG tax would reduce govt revenue by nearly 0.1-0.2% of GDP, a level it said could be absorbed while keeping fiscal deficit targets broadly on track. "We believe govt would be able to take this hit if hypothetically, the entire capital gains taxes were abolished," the report said. articles.title: Canva CEO says a major reorganization will affect 22% of its workforce. Read the memo.
articles.summary: Canva CEO Melanie Perkins wrote a memo explaining how a major reorganization will affect 22% of the company's workforce.
articles.body:
Canva says 1,271 employees — 22% of its workforce — will be affected by a major reorganization.

In a 1,600-word memo, Canva's CEO wrote that it's simplifying ranks and moving more roles to Sydney.

Employees who lose their jobs will get at least six months' pay. The company hasn't said how many will be cut.

Canva has announced a major restructuring.

On Tuesday, the design software company's CEO, Melanie Perkins , published a memo sent to employees titled "An important update on our team." In it, she said that 1,271 employees, roughly 22% of the workforce, will be affected by a reorganization. Some employees will see their roles change or relocate, she said, while others will lose their jobs.

It comes after Canva lowered its growth expectations. In August, the company changed its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20%. In Tuesday's memo, Perkins said that this year has been the company's "hardest year yet" and that "growth has slowed for the first time in a decade."

Canva has also faced fresh competition from AI tools, including OpenAI's and Google's image-generating models.

Hi everyone, Today, I have some profoundly difficult news to share. After months of thinking through how to set Canva up for the next chapter, we have made the incredibly hard decision to make significant changes to how we're organised, where some of our teams are based, and the roles and skills we need for the future. This means 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, will be impacted. For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs. Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today. This is without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history. Behind every decision is someone we care deeply about, and I know the consequences will be very real for those directly affected, their families, friends and teammates. I'm deeply sorry for the pain and disruption this will cause for everyone affected. While nothing can make this news easier, we will do everything we possibly can to support everyone affected. I want to explain as openly as I can why we're making these changes, how we reached these decisions, and, most importantly, how we will care for the people affected today. We've spoken a lot about how quickly the world is changing. New technology is transforming what people can create, how they create it, and what they expect from the products they use. Over the past thirteen years, we've turned a dream in a pitch deck into a platform used by hundreds of millions of people. None of it would have been possible without the talent, imagination and care of every single person who has been part of this journey. Yet success in our first chapter doesn't guarantee success in the next. This has been our hardest year yet, and as we shared earlier this year, our growth has slowed for the first time in a decade. After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I've come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won't be enough. To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership and focus on what matters most for our community. It also means making some of the hardest decisions we've ever faced, including saying goodbye to people who have helped make Canva what it is today. For that, I am deeply sorry. We're making three changes to bring more of what has made Canva special back into how we work. #1. We're simplifying how we come together to build Canva As we've grown, more of our work has become organised around team structures and narrow areas of ownership. Improving one part of our product often requires navigating between Product, Growth and Platform, with more handovers and coordination than necessary. This has made it harder to take ownership of bigger problems and to build a deeply unified product for our community. We've tried many ways to solve this over the years, but it's become clear we need to revisit our underlying structure. To do that, we're bringing Product, Growth and Platform together into one Product Org and changing the way we work to provide clearer ownership, greater autonomy and flexibility to tackle our most important goals. We want to get back to spending more time building, and less time navigating how work gets done. #2. We're reducing subspecialisation and collapsing layers to broaden ownership Over time, we've divided work across more and more subspecialties and teams. While this has helped us build valuable expertise, it's also fragmented ownership and made it harder to see the full picture, with different teams responsible for many pieces of the same work. We're reducing this fragmentation and incorporating narrower subspecialties into broader roles so teams have more ownership of goals from start to finish. We're also simplifying layers, consolidating overlapping responsibilities, and ensuring teams have the right mix of skills and experience for the chapter ahead. #3. We're co-locating closely connected teams and increasing in-person collaboration Working across countries has brought enormous benefits and talent, but it's also made it harder to bring the right people together to solve complex problems. We'll continue investing in our global team, particularly where being close to our community, customers and markets matters most. At the same time, Sydney will become the primary home for more of our product teams, as well as roles in other Specialties where shared context and close collaboration are especially important. We know relocating is a big decision for those being asked to consider it, and we're committed to making the process as smooth as possible with comprehensive support. We also want to bring more teams together in person to build trust, learn from one another and strengthen the connections that make Canva special. From January, we expect most Hybrid Canvanauts to spend around 2 to 3 days in the office each week, depending on what makes sense in your area. I know many of you will have questions about how we made these decisions. We began with one question: what does Canva need to do to succeed in the chapter ahead? We started with our mission and future goals, then considered the structures, skills and locations needed to achieve them. Only then did we look at what this would mean for individual roles. While understanding how we reached these decisions won't make them any less painful, I want to emphasise that they are not a reflection of the talent, care and dedication people have brought to Canva, their skills or the enormous contributions they've made along the way. We know everyone's circumstances are different, and while nothing can make today's news easy, we've tried to reflect those different needs in the financial, career and wellbeing support we're providing to everyone affected: Everyone will receive at least six months of salary, inclusive of statutory entitlements, regardless of location. Removing the one-year vesting cliff for those who joined in the past year. Twelve months of continued healthcare coverage in countries where we currently provide this. Twelve months of Canva Care (our EAP) , with this coverage also extending to family members. Dedicated career support, including one-on-one coaching, interview preparation, and one year of LinkedIn Premium. We're also dedicating a significant portion of our Talent Acquisition team to helping people review their resumes and practice for interviews to find their next opportunity. An opt-in alumni talent directory that we'll proactively share with our investors, partners, and wider industry network to help connect departing Canvanauts with new roles. Everyone leaving will be able to keep their Canva MacBook as we know not everyone has a personal laptop. We're also launching the Canva Collective Fund, providing US$10,000 grants to departing Canvanauts who want to start something of their own. Whether it's starting a business or doing something meaningful for their local community, the fund is designed to help get those ideas off the ground. Everyone leaving as part of these changes will have until the 14 of December to register their interest, and we won't take any ownership or equity in what they create. Our immediate priority is to make time for the conversations with everyone directly impacted by these changes. Those impacted will receive a calendar invite for an individual meeting with a senior leader in their area to discuss the next steps and support available should they wish to attend. With teams across 37 countries, we'll need to follow different local requirements and processes, which means the timing and way these conversations happen may vary depending on where people are based. We also want to give everyone the time to process this news and say goodbye in their own way. Everyone leaving Canva will continue to have access to Slack and Gmail until the end of the week, so they can choose when and how to share the news with their teams. This means you may not know exactly how your team is changing straight away, and we ask everyone to respect the privacy of those having these conversations. There's no need to read through everything right now, but we hope they'll be helpful whenever you're ready. We've asked Org Leads to wait until after this to bring their teams together, with Org All Hands taking place from November 11th. To everyone continuing at Canva: I know this news will be incredibly difficult, especially as we say goodbye to friends and teammates who have been such an important part of our journey. There's no need to log this as leave. To those who will be leaving Canva: I wish I could adequately express how grateful I am for everything you've contributed. The Canva that exists today is the result of your hard work, creativity, passion and care. Hundreds of millions of people around the world have been empowered by what you've helped build, and I hope you know just how much of a difference you've made. I am deeply sorry this is how your chapter at Canva is ending. Please know these decisions do not diminish your talent, the value of your contributions, or the difference you've made here.
